body.name: \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\)
body.construction: Accept only a tuple certified by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), and construct the finite family of rational circuits \(T_{D,y}\) and polynomial signatures \(F_{D,y}\).  Compute the zero or nonzero status of each fixed-order normal form \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})\) by exact real-radical membership or its equivalent real-closed-field decision.  If every normal form is zero, output the reference circuit \((T_{D_0,y})_y\) together with finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities.  Otherwise first test the supplied rational exact-oracle witness \(p^{\circ}\); if some \(F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq0\), return \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\).  For every remaining pair \((D,y)\) with nonzero normal form, in canonical order decide the basic semialgebraic formula \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) and \(F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\) by a fixed exact real-closed-field quantifier-elimination or cylindrical algebraic decomposition procedure.  At the first feasible formula, return \((D_0,D,p^\dagger)\), where \(p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega\) is encoded by a rational univariate representation, coordinate minimal polynomials, and isolating or Thom data.  If every such formula is infeasible, output the reference circuit, using real-radical identities for the zero-normal-form pairs and finite quantifier-elimination traces or Positivstellensatz identities for the remaining pairs.  A nonzero normal form is only a trigger for the positive-chamber feasibility test and is never itself reported as an ambiguity certificate.
